title: The Hollow of the Glass Steppe Revisited
premise: Emrys Lockridge, last apprentice of the Wardwrights' Guild, has spent their whole life in Vael Hollow, a valley where magic cannot cross the border wards. On the night the stars vanish, the wards shatter, and the hollow's long-exiled founders return as hollowed, starless revenants demanding the covenant be repaid in blood. Emrys must journey into the glass steppe with a found family of outcasts to reforge the covenant at the First Hearth. In the end, Emrys learns the covenant was never about sacrifice but about welcome, and by choosing to belong to both worlds rather than either, they relight the stars and give the hollow a future beyond its walls.
about_author: Mara Galloway is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing border-town folklore before turning to fiction. They write quiet, aching fantasies about people who were never meant to be heroes.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgot the Sky
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. A quiet portrait of Vael Hollow and the guild's last days: Emrys tends the border wards alone, memorizing rituals their dead master never finished teaching. When a wardstone hums a note Emrys has never heard, unease settles in. Emotional beat: longing disguised as contentment.

chapters.title: Nine Candles for the Guild
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The guild's autumn remembrance; nine names read aloud, only Emrys left to answer. Old Wren, the guild's half-mad retired mender, hints that the covenant has a second clause no one wrote down. Emotional beat: grief as inheritance.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The stars vanish in a single breath, and every wardstone in the hollow cracks at once. In the sudden dark, Emrys sees figures crossing the border where nothing living should pass. Emotional beat: terror and the end of the known world.

chapters.title: What Walked Out of the Steppe
chapters.summary: Alternating Emrys and Wren. The revenants—hollowed founders with starless eyes—deliver an ultimatum at the guild door: the covenant's debt is due by the winter solstice, or the hollow is unmade. Emotional beat: the past arriving with a bill.

chapters.title: A Ledger of Debts
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Searching the guild archive, Emrys finds the original covenant fragment: a promise of 'hearth and hand' that later guilds rewrote into sacrifice. The council votes to pay the old way—with a life. Emotional beat: betrayal by one's own people.

chapters.title: The Council's Choice
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The council names Emrys, the last wardwright, as the acceptable payment. Wren publicly defies them and is cast out. Emrys, cornered between duty and self, chooses to run—not to flee the debt, but to find another answer. Emotional beat: the first act of rebellion.

chapters.title: Outcasts at the Broken Gate
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. At the border ruins Emrys gathers unlikely companions: Wren; Sable, a smuggler who knows the steppe; and Idris, a revenant who refused hollowing and still remembers his name. Emotional beat: the fragile first stitches of found family.

chapters.title: Crossing the Glass
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The party crosses the steppe's mirror flats, where reflections show who you were, not who you are. Sable navigates by her own shame. Emrys sees their reflection smile without them. Emotional beat: confronting what you abandoned.

chapters.title: The Waystation of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. The group shelters with a community of steppe-dwellers who were exiled from the hollow generations ago—people the wards were built to keep out. Idris recognizes the cost of his people's hunger. Emotional beat: belonging refused, then offered.

chapters.title: What the Revenants Remember
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. Idris reveals the truth: the founders hollowed themselves willingly when the hollow's fear-starved wards cut them off from the hearth-magic that sustained them. The debt is real, but the payment was always misread. Emotional beat: horror softened into pity.

chapters.title: The Hollowing of Wren
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A starless wind catches Wren, and she begins to forget—first the guild's names, then her own. Emrys holds her through the night, reciting her memories back to her. Emotional beat: love as an act of resistance against erasure.

chapters.title: The First Hearth, Cold
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The party reaches the First Hearth, the covenant's origin, and finds it dead—its flame stolen, its keepers long gone. The solstice is nine days off. Emrys realizes relighting it requires a living covenant, not a corpse. Emotional beat: the plan collapses.

chapters.title: Sable's Price
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable confesses she once smuggled wardstone out of the hollow, cracking it from inside; her guilt is the wound the steppe's mirrors showed. She offers her smugglers' network as the map to the stolen flame. Emotional beat: guilt transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Court of Ash and Salt
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The flame's thief is revealed: the hollow council's first speaker, still alive, who took the fire believing the covenant was a cage. He offers Emrys a bargain: let the hollow stay warded and blind, safe and small, forever. Emotional beat: temptation of comfortable cowardice.

chapters.title: The Bargain Refused
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys refuses—not with heroics but with the archive's original words: 'hearth and hand.' The covenant was hospitality, not sacrifice. The thief's court turns on them, and the party flees with the flame and a wound. Emotional beat: conviction tested and held.

chapters.title: Nine Days to Solstice
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. A desperate race back across the steppe as the hollowed revenants, sensing the flame, converge. Idris begins to hollow again to buy time. Emotional beat: every step costs something irreplaceable.

chapters.title: The Gate Holds, Barely
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The party reaches the border to find the hollow council sealing it—choosing blindness over reckoning. Wren, half-hollowed, speaks the founders' true names and shames the wards open. Emotional beat: the excluded one becomes the key.

chapters.title: Solstice Eve
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. At the guild hall, Emrys lays out the covenant's original text before the hollow's people and the revenants alike. The council's speaker confesses the theft. Emrys asks not for a sacrifice but for everyone's hand. Emotional beat: the quiet before the choice.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. At the First Hearth's echo in the hollow's center, Emrys relights the flame by giving it what no one offered before: welcome, spoken in both tongues, hollow and steppe. Idris's hollowing halts; the revenants weep their names back. Emotional beat: love against duty, duty transformed.

chapters.title: The Stars Return
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The stars reignite one by one over the steppe, and the border wards dissolve—not broken, but no longer needed. The hollow must decide who it is without walls. Emotional beat: awe, and the vertigo of freedom.

chapters.title: A Guild With Open Doors
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Spring: the guild reopens as a school for wardwrights and steppe-folk alike, with Wren teaching, Sable charting, and Idris as the first student from beyond the border. Emrys writes the covenant's new first line. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not inherited.

chapters.title: The Hollow of the Glass Steppe
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV, years later. Emrys stands at the old border, now a road, watching travelers pass freely between worlds. A child asks what the hollow was like when the stars were gone. Emrys answers honestly: it was small, and it was home, and it learned to be more. Emotional beat: peace earned and passed on.
